subtype: Approach: root-cause analysis with five whys [Thinking]
passage: Note, Wednesday, by Pema, Maths teacher. Pranav stayed after class with his failed test and said, "I will find out why myself." He wrote on the board: Why did I fail? Because I could not solve the equations. Why? Because I got the algebra steps wrong. Why? Because I do not handle negative signs and brackets well. Why? Because my Class 8 basics in fractions and algebra are weak. Why did I skip those? Because I passed Class 8 and never went back. He turned and said, "It is not this chapter. It is the foundation." I added nothing. I offered him Class 8 practice sheets, and he took two.

qa.q: What did Pranav conclude was the root of the problem?
qa.a: He concluded that the weak fractions and algebra basics from Class 8 were the root.

qa.q: What might Pranav have felt when he reached the last "why"?
qa.a: Relieved to find a fixable cause, though perhaps uncomfortable about having skipped the basics.
Work through Class 8 practice sheets in short sessions, then return to the current chapter, because the foundation supports it.

qa.q: How might Pema see Pranav's self-analysis?
qa.a: As a strong sign of ownership, since Pema added nothing and only offered practice sheets.

grounding: A student failing Maths asks why repeatedly and traces the trouble back to weak Class 8 basics, not the current chapter.
